newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's Koncar to float abroad 30 pct of shares.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Koncar to float abroad 30 pct of shares.

text.p: Croatia's electrical concern Koncar Elektroindustrija on Tuesday agreed for Zagrebacka Banka and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to help it float over 30 percent of shares on international market.
Koncar plans to offer abroad 31.16 percent of its capital, or 216,000 shares, for 108 million German marks in about a year.
Another 180,000 shares have been intended for distribution to war veterans and refugees as a part of a mass voucher privatisation scheme.

"This contract... will help offer abroad 31.16 percent of Koncar's shares, that will hopefully follow in the footsteps of (leading drugs firm) Pliva to the world market," Croatian Privatisation Minister Milan Kovac told a news conference.

Koncar and the state Privatisation Fund (HPF) on Tuesday signed an agreement with Croatia's leading bank, Zagrebacka Banka, and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) to help the firm's privatisation as financial advisers .

"One of the key issues... is to have a broad and stable ownership structure. Over 30 percent of the capital owned by international investors should guarantee stability..," a DMG's director, Adrian Ball, told journalists.

Croatian government had first privatised Pliva through a global flotation in March 1996. Pliva's Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) now trade on London Stock Exchange and they traded in a $16.15-16.475 range on Tuesday.

Koncar soon plans to list its shares in the top segment of the Zagreb bourse, alongside Pliva, Zagrebacka and Varazdinska Banka. It also wants to create GDRs for listing on one or more international stock exchanges.
"Roadshows will start some eight to nine months after the first, analytical phase begins," Ball told Reuters.

Milivoj Goldstein of Zagrebacka said his bank and DMG hoped to help Koncar become a majority-privatised company which would attract international and local investors and expand its share in the world market.
A total of 396,000 shares to be offered to Croatian and foreign investors will come from the HPF's portfolio, which has so far controlled 60.74 percent of Koncar.
Pension funds would retain some 30 percent in the firm and small shareholders would control 7.20 percent.
A tiny stake in the firm, whose equity is valued at 365 million marks, is held by the German electrical giant Siemens.
Ball said DMG would help Koncar work on its comparative advantages to attract potential international investors.
"Koncar is more difficult than Pliva. It is easier to sell pharmaceuticals... But there is definitely a market for a firm like Koncar," Ball said.
Koncar said its 1996 sales topped one million kuna, 30 percent of which were exports. It plans to increase sales by 70 percent in the next five years. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
